records.reference: Last Saturday the community library held a reading day. Older children read stories to younger visitors. Volunteers helped choose books and make bookmarks. Over fifty families came and many borrowed books. The library plans a reading afternoon every month.

I used to rush out of the house without breakfast. Now I prepare my schoolbag before going to bed. I have enough time to eat, check my homework and walk to school. A small change has made my mornings much calmer.

My grandfather taught me how to mend a loose button. At first I found it difficult to hold the needle. After a few tries, I could do it by myself. I was proud that I did not have to throw away my shirt.

There is a small reading corner beside our classroom window. Students can sit there during the lunch break. We take turns looking after the books, and everyone is asked to speak quietly. It is my favourite place on a busy school day.

During a cooking lesson, I added too much salt to the soup. My partner suggested adding more water and vegetables. The soup tasted better in the end. I learned that a mistake can become a chance to find a solution together.

On Sunday, my aunt showed me how to make dumplings. She prepared the filling while I rolled out the dough. We made some unusual shapes, but they tasted delicious. By the time we finished, the whole kitchen smelled wonderful.

Our neighbour noticed that the path was slippery after the rain. He brought a broom and cleared the wet leaves away. Soon the children could walk past safely. It reminded me that looking after shared spaces is everyone's responsibility.

While cleaning a cupboard, I found an old map of our town. Many of the streets still had the same names, but several buildings had disappeared. My father showed me where he used to play as a child. The map helped me see our town differently.

Our class built a model bridge from paper. One group made the base while another tested its strength. We changed our design when it began to bend. At the end of the lesson, the bridge could hold several small books without breaking.

I planted a bean seed in a paper cup and kept it near the window. For several days nothing seemed to happen. Then a tiny green leaf appeared. Watching it grow taught me to be patient and to notice small changes in nature.

A new student joined our class last month. At lunchtime she often sat alone, so we invited her to join our table. We discovered that she enjoyed drawing animals as much as we did. Soon we were sharing ideas for a class poster.

The wall near our school used to be plain and grey. A group of students planned a picture of birds, trees and flowers. Local residents helped paint it over a weekend. Now the wall makes the street brighter, and people often stop to look at it.

My grandmother showed me a letter she wrote when she was my age. She described her school and the games she played with friends. Some things were different, but her excitement about learning felt familiar. Reading the letter brought us closer together.

Before our class presentation, I was afraid of forgetting my words. My partner reminded me to look at the audience and speak slowly. When I finished, I realised that I had enjoyed sharing our ideas. The next time I felt much more confident.

Our town has a path along the river. Volunteers often collect rubbish left by visitors. They also put up signs to remind people to take their litter home. A clean river is important for wildlife and for everyone who enjoys walking beside it.

Last summer, my family stayed in a village instead of visiting a large city. We walked through fields, bought fruit from a small market and watched the stars at night. We did not make a busy timetable. It was one of the most relaxing holidays I can remember.

I noticed how many plastic bags we used each week. Now I carry a cloth bag when I go shopping. I also refill my water bottle rather than buying a new one. These simple habits help me create less waste without changing my daily life very much.

While walking in the park, I noticed a bird building its nest. I stood at a distance and watched it carry small pieces of grass into a tree. I did not disturb it. Seeing the bird at work made an ordinary walk much more interesting.

Last Saturday I left my phone at home and met two friends in the park. We played a ball game and talked for a long time. I did not miss my phone as much as I expected. Spending time together was more enjoyable than looking at a screen.
